memory_candidates.insight: When a multi-phase Lean plan pins each phase's exit signatures as Challenge statements, a final assembly phase that needs NO new lemma, no induction, and only the case split the statement itself forces is positive evidence that the decomposition was correct. The converse is the diagnostic worth watching for: if an assembly phase has to introduce new mathematics, some earlier phase's pinned statement was the wrong statement, and the right response is to question that statement rather than to grow the assembly.

A probe or evidence file built up across many dispatches accumulates FALSE header prose: a header written at phase 2 saying 'nothing in this file yet mentions X' stays in place while later phases land X. The staleness is invisible to every compile and every sorry census, because it is inside a comment. Worth an explicit header re-read at the phase that lands the file's headline, and worth correcting additively rather than leaving a file whose own header misdescribes it.

A bounded waiter on a detached local command must use the sentinel pattern (the command appends a marker such as 'GUARD_EXIT=$?' to its own log; the waiter greps for that marker) or kill -0 on a captured PID -- never 'pgrep -f <name>'. A pgrep-based predicate silently fails to observe completion and burns the waiter's entire timeout while the watched command has already finished green. Observed cost: 600s lost on a census that had already exited 0.
